title: Digital Safety, Privacy, and Your Digital Footprint

questions.question: Which of these is part of your passive digital footprint?
options: Tracking cookies collected as you browse
A comment you type on a video
An email you send to a friend
questions.rationale: Passive traces are collected without deliberate action on your part — cookies, IP logs, and location pings — while posts and comments are active footprints.

questions.question: For passwords, which principle contributes most to crack resistance?
options: Length combined with uniqueness and randomness
Using your birthday as a base
Adding one exclamation mark to a dictionary word
questions.rationale: Every extra random character multiplies the search space enormously, and uniqueness stops one breach from unlocking all your accounts.

questions.question: Why should you never reuse passwords across important sites?
options: Reused passwords trigger account locks everywhere
One site's breach leaks credentials tried on every other site you use
questions.rationale: Credential stuffing replays leaked email-password pairs against other services, so uniqueness confines a breach to the site that was hit.

questions.question: A password manager's core job is to:
options: Generate and store strong unique passwords behind one master password
Block phishing emails at the server
questions.rationale: The vault generates random per-site passwords and autofills them, so you only need to protect one strong master password.

questions.question: A login that asks for your password and a six-digit code from an authenticator app uses which factor combination?
questions.rationale: The password is something you know and the app-generated code is something you possess — two different families, which is what makes it genuine MFA.

questions.question: Which second-factor method is considered the most phishing-resistant?
options: Hardware security keys such as FIDO2 keys
questions.rationale: Hardware keys cryptographically bind the login to the genuine site domain, so a lookalike phishing page cannot capture and replay the response.

questions.question: The main weakness of SMS-based one-time codes is:
options: SIM-swap attacks let criminals receive your messages
They only work on rooted phones
They cost the user money per login
questions.rationale: In a SIM swap the attacker transfers your number to their SIM and receives your codes, which is why authenticator apps and security keys are preferred.

questions.question: India's principal cyber law, which gives legal recognition to electronic records and defines offences like identity theft under Section 66C, is the:
questions.rationale: The IT Act 2000, amended in 2008, is India's baseline cyber statute; the DPDP Act 2023 supplements it for personal-data handling.

questions.question: CERT-In, constituted in 2004 under Section 70B of the IT Act, is responsible for:
options: National cyber incident response, alerts, and advisories
questions.rationale: CERT-In is India's national incident response agency — it issues advisories, coordinates breach response, and mandates six-hour incident reporting for service providers.

questions.question: Data minimisation as a privacy habit means:
options: Sharing the least data needed, with the fewest parties, for the shortest time
Posting everything in one large archive
questions.rationale: The footprint you never create cannot leak or be profiled, so limiting data shared in scope, audience, and retention is the core habit.
